name: TeamStarWolf - Instructure Canvas Breach 2026 Case Study
description: Curated case-study layer, not an official MITRE mapping. Enterprise ATT&CK v20.0 techniques bound in the Instructure Canvas breach case study: the Free-for-Teacher account and support ticket of April 2026, the cross-site scripting that gave the actor a support agent's token, the bulk collection, the ransom note on login pages of 7 May 2026 and the extortion that ended in the agreement of 11 May, with the September 2025 Salesforce compromise as context. No source names ATT&CK ids, so every binding is the study's own reading. Score 100: a primary states the behavior and the technique fits directly. Score 60: the fit is partly inferred. Scores measure the strength of the tie to this record, not severity. No malware, tool or exfiltration channel is in the record, so none is bound. Comments carry the study's source numbers.

Exploit Public-Facing Application. Cross-site scripting in a support ticket (April 2026) and in the discussion feature (7 May 2026); a partial fit, since the flaw sits in the public-facing service but ran in a support agent's browser. Sources: [1] [2].
Data from Information Repositories. The actor claims DAP queries, provisioning reports and user APIs (5 May 2026); the vendor's July 2026 deliveries match those categories. Sources: [1] [18].
External Defacement. Ransom note on login pages through custom-theme CSS, visible to roughly 300 organizations, 7 May 2026. Sources: [1] [2] [19].
Steal Application Access Token. Authorization token taken from the support agent's session (April 2026); a token generated through the OAuth flow on 7 May 2026. Sources: [2].
Application Access Token. The stolen token used for elevated access within Canvas, April 2026. Sources: [2].
Establish Accounts. A Free-for-Teacher account created to file the support ticket, April 2026; a partial fit, since the account was made on the victim's own free tier. Sources: [2].
Financial Theft. Extortion: ransom note with a 12 May deadline (7 May 2026) and the agreement of 11 May 2026. Sources: [1] [2] [19].
Social Engineering. The September 2025 compromise of Instructure's Salesforce instance, a separate earlier incident; the vendor names no channel, so no sub-technique. Sources: [7].
